label: late original-phase steps and the <DEL> step (end of input reading)
explanation: Fires only while the sequence is being read in: original-phase steps from position 3-4 onward and the <DEL> step itself (32% of mass; active on 48% of delimiter steps). Never fires at t<=2 and essentially never in the copy phase (1 step of 2.7M). Firing rate rises with orig_idx (8% at pos 3 up to 69% at pos 8) and with L, so the longest sequences carry most mass. It prefers first occurrences of a token (in_first=1 holds 90% of mass). Within the window it is far from always on (precision about 0.45), and which steps fire depends on token content: rate is higher when the early tokens include z, x, c, 0, e, o, 1, n (first_tok z: 2.0x lift), and when the current input is b, p, s. Adding that early-token condition raises F1 only from 0.61 to 0.66, so it is left out of the predicate. Top activations (about 6.7) come at the last original token or two of 8-9 token sequences (often b/p) and at the following <DEL>.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: z, x, c, 0, o, e; least: s, i, p, b) and the current input token, by phase (input phase: b, p, s, i; delimiter step: <DEL>; copy phase: q); timing cues that raise it most: t=6, t=7, t=5.
